passage:
Jomon, put that phone down a moment. I'm Raghav, and I want to tell you about a night when I was twenty. A message reached our hostel group: a photo of a tea-stall owner supposedly beating a child, and the words “Share until he's shamed.” Thirty of us boys were furious. Somebody said, “Let's go to the stall now.”

My thumb was over the share button. Something made me pause. I asked, “Where was this taken?” Nobody knew. I rang Suresh, whose family lives near that stall. “The stall is closed for a wedding,” he said. “The old man is at home.”

The photo turned out to be from another town, years old. Afterwards I thought about the tea-stall owner, Manohar, who never knew how close a crowd had come. I still wait ten minutes before I share anything.

qa.q: What did Raghav ask when the message arrived?
qa.a: Raghav asked, “Where was this taken?”

qa.q: Why did Raghav pause with a thumb over the share button?
qa.a: Despite the group's fury, Raghav felt uneasy and doubtful, and wanted to know the source first, since a photo without a place or date proved nothing.

qa.q: What did Raghav do to check the message before sharing?
qa.a: Raghav rang Suresh, whose family lives near the stall, and learned the stall was closed and the owner was at home.

qa.q: What might have happened to Manohar if the crowd had gone to the stall that night?
qa.a: Manohar, an innocent old man, could have been frightened or hurt by an angry crowd over a false photo, without ever knowing why.

grounding: A young adult checks the source of a viral accusation before sharing, and the pause breaks the chain that turns anger into a mob.

passage:
Sangeeta's bus was three stops from home, and her phone said 5%. A video was flooding the residents' group: a delivery man supposedly stealing from a parcel locker, angry messages piling up beneath it. Yogesh had already typed, “Report him to the police right now!”

Her thumb hovered over the share button. She felt her own anger rising. Then she took one slow breath and tapped the username on the video. It was a new account. She searched the caption, and the same clip appeared from another city, months old, with a different story.

“Yogesh, wait,” she typed. “This video is old and from somewhere else. Let's check before we name anyone.”

The phone died before he replied. At her stop she saw that the group had gone quiet.

qa.q: What did Sangeeta's phone say when the bus was three stops from home?
qa.a: Sangeeta's phone said 5%.

qa.q: What was Sangeeta feeling when the thumb hovered over the share button?
qa.a: Sangeeta felt anger rising, yet paused to breathe before acting.

qa.q: What steps did Sangeeta take before sharing the video?
qa.a: Sangeeta tapped the username, saw a new account, searched the caption and found the same clip from another city, months old.

qa.q: How might the delivery man have been affected if the video had kept spreading?
qa.a: The delivery man could have been wrongly named and shamed, or even threatened, for something never done.

grounding: A young adult under time pressure checks the source of a viral accusation before sharing, breaking the chain that turns anger into a mob.

passage:
Tushar's phone buzzed during his lunch break in the Bengaluru office. A viral post: a café owner in Indiranagar slapping a delivery boy, with the café's name in the caption. Two thousand shares in an hour. His finger hovered over share. He was furious.
Then he stopped. Something about the video looked off. The signs in the background weren't in Kannada or English.
He spent four minutes searching. The same clip had been posted three years ago from another country. The café in the caption had nothing to do with it.
He texted Preeti, who had already shared it. “Check this, it's fake. Wrong café.” Preeti replied, “Oh no. Deleting.” Tushar posted the original link under the viral post. By evening, the café owner's reply was pinned at the top.

qa.q: How many shares did the post have in an hour?
qa.a: It had two thousand shares in an hour.

qa.q: What was Tushar feeling when his finger hovered over share?
qa.a: He was furious and ready to share, but something felt off and made him pause.

qa.q: What did Tushar's four-minute pause achieve?
qa.a: It revealed the clip was old and from another country, so he stopped the chain and helped Preeti and others correct it.

qa.q: How might the café owner have felt before the correction?
qa.a: The owner was probably frightened and angry, falsely accused in front of thousands.

grounding: Shows a young man pausing to check the source of a viral accusation before sharing, which breaks the chain of outrage.

passage:
“Rekha, did you see this? Sharing it right now,” Rajni said, holding up her phone in the hostel room. “Professor Iyer said girls shouldn't do engineering! Screenshot from his class group!”
Rekha frowned. “Wait. Before you share. Who posted it?”
“Some page. Doesn't matter. Look at it!”
“It does matter. Give me two minutes.”
Rekha zoomed in. “The font in the second line is different. And the date says Sunday. He doesn't message the class on Sundays.”
Rajni hesitated. “Maybe.”
Rekha messaged a friend in his class. Reply: “Fake. He never said that.”
Rajni put down her phone slowly. “I was so angry. I almost sent it to three groups.”

qa.q: What did the date on the screenshot say?
qa.a: The date said Sunday.

qa.q: How did Rajni feel before Rekha stopped her?
qa.a: She felt angry and outraged, ready to send it to three groups.

qa.q: What small step did Rekha take, and why did it matter?
qa.a: Rekha asked for two minutes to check the source and messaged a classmate, which showed the screenshot was fake before it spread.

qa.q: How might Professor Iyer have been affected if Rajni had shared it?
qa.a: He could have been falsely accused and attacked by angry students for something he never said.

grounding: Shows a student pausing to check a viral screenshot before sharing, which stops a friend's anger from joining a pile-on.

passage:
I'm Mohit, and one evening last year, I nearly helped start something terrible.
A video came into our colony group: a man in a cap walking near the school, and a message saying he was a child kidnapper, with a photo of a local vegetable seller who looked a bit similar. People were furious. Someone wrote, “Let's find him tonight.”
My cousin Jaya had already forwarded it to two more groups. My thumb was on forward too.
Then I stopped. I searched the words of the message. The same text had been going round in three other states, with different photos. The police page had a notice calling it false.
I posted the police notice in the group and called Jaya. She deleted her forwards. The vegetable seller was at his cart the next morning, safe.

qa.q: Who did the photo in the message show?
qa.a: It showed a local vegetable seller who looked a bit similar.

qa.q: How did Mohit feel looking back on that evening?
qa.a: Mohit feels shaken and relieved, knowing the pause nearly didn't happen.

qa.q: Why was Mohit's pause so important?
qa.a: Checking the message showed it was a false rumour, and posting the police notice stopped an angry group from turning into a mob.

qa.q: How might the vegetable seller have been affected if nobody had checked?
qa.a: He could have been attacked by an angry crowd for something he never did.

grounding: A young adult recalls pausing to check a viral accusation before forwarding it, which broke the chain before anger became a mob.

passage:
Warden's note, Boys' Hostel B, Saturday.
Around 10 p.m. a message went round the hostel groups: a photo of a delivery man with the caption "This man tried to break into rooms in Block C. Share and catch him!" Within minutes about twenty students had gathered in the common room, some talking about waiting at the gate to "deal with him" tomorrow.
Nilesh, a second-year, didn't forward it. He zoomed into the photo and said, "Hang on. That's not our gate. And this post is from last year." Salma, on a video call from the other campus, confirmed it was an old photo from a different city. The check took about five minutes. The room went quiet.
What I did next: I posted in every hostel group that the claim was false, asked the admins to remove it, and reminded everyone to bring worries to the warden's office, not the gate.

qa.q: About how long did the check take?
qa.a: About five minutes.

qa.q: What was Nilesh probably feeling as others talked about the gate?
qa.a: Nilesh was likely uneasy and doubtful, not willing to join the anger before knowing whether the post was true.

qa.q: Why was the warden's follow-up important?
qa.a: Correcting it in every group and removing the post stopped the rumour spreading further and pointed students to a safe channel.

qa.q: What would have changed for the delivery man if nobody had paused?
qa.a: He could have been confronted or hurt at the gate for something he never did.

grounding: Shows a young adult checking the source of a viral accusation before sharing it, and how a short pause breaks the chain toward a mob.
